scopeReview: IMP-5.C.1: geographic variation in women’s food-production, distribution and consumption roles across production types. Distinguishes participation, registered ownership, management, access and decision-making; includes agency and cooperative leadership alongside structural constraints, without fixed gender stereotypes.
varietyReview: Four meaningful stimuli:work versus owner denominators, three-stage worker bars, credit applications/rates and original management-share map across production regions. Checks independently compute60%/20%, task-specific shares,50%/75% approval and north/south contrast. Qualitative source/scale cases assess omitted work, mobility and decision measurement.
repetitionReview: Different denominators and evidence types prevent work, ownership, task shares, applicant rates and operation management being conflated. No global factual percentages or earlier time-use clone. Original synthetic examples, varied keys and all-option explanations; difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: FAO primary synthesis verified the relevance of resource access, unpaid work and varied agrifood roles. All counts, regions and programs fictional, not copied statistics; no personal data or real credit eligibility decision. No resource addition or independent human-review claim.

questions.correctOption: Women are 60% of recorded agricultural workers but 20% of registered landowners; participation and registered ownership are different measures.
questions.independentReview: Independently calculated90/150=.60 and10/50=.20. Registers are separate universes, not necessarily disjoint; no assumption that owner counts measure hectares, secure customary rights or decision authority.

questions.correctOption: Women are a majority in planting and selling, but a minority in packing.
questions.independentReview: Independently checked women’s stage shares60%,10%,80%. Each denominator100 is supplied; role groups may overlap, so no total unique population is obtained by adding all role counts.

questions.correctOption: Women receive more approvals in total, but their approval rate is 50%, below men’s 75%.
questions.independentReview: Independently recomputed50% versus75% and40>15. Denominator is applicants, not all farmers or all women/men in the community. No causal discrimination finding or actual credit decision inferred.

questions.correctOption: Women manage larger shares of operations in the northern gardening districts, but location and production type vary together and do not isolate a cause.
questions.independentReview: Checked each northvalue65/55 exceeds each southvalue25/35, and map values are shares of operations managed, not shares of female residents employed. Fictional regional mix cannot establish biological traits, universal roles or an independent causal crop effect.

questions.correctOption: Unpaid family production, processing and marketing work may be missed when only paid jobs and one respondent’s status are counted.
questions.independentReview: FAO measurement themes checked; no global labor percentage or assumption that every household head is male. The concern follows the stated survey exclusions.

questions.correctOption: Labor mobility can reshape agricultural roles, but the extent and associated rights need local evidence.
questions.independentReview: Separated migration-associated responsibility from automatic empowerment or ownership. No claim that every male migrant leaves permanently or that all remaining women experience the same changes.

questions.correctOption: Women’s contributions can extend across production, processing, marketing and collective decision-making.
questions.independentReview: Aligned IMP-5.C.1 food production/distribution/consumption and variation by production type. Agency and leadership retained; no stereotype that women only perform subsistence labor.

questions.correctOption: Attendance alone proves all participants acquired secure land rights and equal control over farm income.
questions.independentReview: Kept an improved participation indicator distinct from ownership or empowerment measures. No causal effect size or universal care role assigned.

questions.correctOption: The groups face different production conditions, so the comparison does not isolate the proposed innate cause.
questions.independentReview: Avoided introducing a real sex-based yield gap or claiming any intervention is guaranteed to close it. The correct logic follows unequal observed conditions, not an unsupported biological assertion.

questions.correctOption: Disaggregation by region, production type and task, with clear denominators and attention to paid and unpaid work.
questions.independentReview: Directly matched official geographic-variation objective. No global average substituted for local evidence; clear categories avoid mixing women’s share of workers with all women’s employment rate.

questions.correctOption: Records of who participates in crop, spending and sale decisions, alongside ownership and work information.
questions.independentReview: Checked outcome-to-measure alignment and preserved joint as well as individual decision possibilities. No universal inference from household title, membership or hours to power.
